title: Signed Calibration Snapshots and Delta Publish Protocol for Reproducible Quant Profiles
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: FP8/INT8 calibration artifacts (profiles, scale tables, per-layer params) are currently stored as opaque blobs without tamper-evident provenance. This makes reproducibility, secure rollback, and validation during rollouts error-prone.

Proposal: Define a signed calibration snapshot format plus an efficient delta-publish protocol. Each snapshot is content-addressable, KMS-signed, and includes a compact manifest with deterministic fields: model_commit, training-config-hash, calibration-seed, dataset-hash, tool-version, quant-profile-schema-version, and per-tensor byte-level hashes. Deltas encode only changed tensors (binary diffs) and reference parent snapshot hash to allow efficient storage and quick verification.

Goals:
- Cryptographic integrity (detect accidental corruption or malicious modification).
- Deterministic snapshot creation (bit-for-bit identical on repeat runs given same inputs).
- Efficient storage & network transfer via deltas.
- Verify-and-validate pipeline before production rollouts with golden-eval harness and checksum-based gating.
- Clear rollback playbook that is KMS-audited and automated where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot format v1 spec committed to docs (fields, canonical serialization, hash algorithm)
KMS signing integration: sign/verify flow for snapshots using customer or Redwood keys
Delta publish tool implemented in calibration service to produce chained deltas and restore full snapshots
CI regression: create snapshot from calibration run, re-run same calibration, verify identical snapshot hash
Release pipeline: pre-rollout validation job that runs golden eval on a pinned sample and gates rollout on accuracy thresholds or fails back to previous signed snapshot
steps: Draft snapshot manifest schema and canonical JSON -> RFC and internal review
Prototype content-addressable serialization (canonical ordering + BLAKE2b + sha256 fallback) and compute cost estimates
Implement sign/verify endpoints in calibration-service; wire KMS for Redwood-managed and customer-provided keys
Add delta encoder/decoder (binary patch) and storage layout for S3 with object tags: snapshot-hash, parent-hash, model-commit
Integrate verification step into deployment flow; add golden-eval job and threshold config in console
Author rollback runbook and automated playbook for safe rollback with signature verification and smoke-tests
comments: 2025-02-11 Maya Singh: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed canonical serialization -> compact msgpack optional but canonical JSON v2 required for human inspection. Use BLAKE2b256 for primary fingerprint (speed) and include SHA256 for cross-tool compatibility.

2025-02-14 Luis Ortega: PoC shows identical snapshots when calibration seed and dataset-hash are fixed. Edge-case: floating-point nondeterminism observed with different MKL/Kernel versions. Action: capture runtime-kernel-metadata and tool-version in snapshot manifest.

2025-02-18 Design review (Jenny Park): Suggested UI surface in Console to show snapshot chain and allow manual signature verification per snapshot. Also request UX for 'force-deploy' with explicit risk acknowledgement.
2025-02-21 Security review kickoff (Asha Patel): KMS key rotation and least-privilege signing principal required. Need threat model doc and A/V for potential rollback abuse scenarios.

2025-02-25 Engineering sync: Decided on delta format: store per-tensor zlib-compressed XOR-diff blocks + metadata; deltas may reference multiple parents for tree-optimized storage in long-lived branches.

2025-02-28 CI run: Created snapshot from calibration job #4056 (model commit abc123). Re-run recreated identical hash on runner with pinned docker image. Filed ENG-24732 to capture flaky host kernel discovery and ENV pinning.

2025-03-02 Luis Ortega: Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/calibration-service/pull/129 implementing manifest writer and verifier. Requesting early security review and integration test task assignment.
